title: Removed locks can hide missing verification and source applicability
observed: Molder 8: apply an Electrical lock without zero-energy verification, remove it, authorize release as Alex, and close the event. All actions are accepted. A separate domain probe records only Hydraulic on a machine whose listed energy sources are Hydraulic and Electrical; acknowledgment and release do not require a job-level decision on the other source.
why: The selected goal concerns complete isolation evidence. The current gates inspect active/applied locks, not historical required verification or an explicit set of task-applicable sources. This can produce a complete-looking closed record with an unverified isolation. A source listed on a machine is not automatically applicable to every task; that applicability must be explicit rather than guessed.
classification: Requirements issue: FR-020(a) requires removed locks and authorization, while (b) checks zero energy only on currently applied locks at handover. The implementation follows that narrow rule. The broader selected completeness goal is not fully translated into the rule.
change: Define task-applicable energy sources and required isolation evidence. Require retained verifier identity/time and all applicable completion fields at release/closeout, even after removal. Show each missing field. Keep active-isolation handover distinct from eventual release; do not demand lock removal merely to hand over.
retest: Remove an unverified lock and attempt release/closure: missing verification must be listed. Omit an applicable source: a missing-source decision must be listed. Valid verified active isolation must still support the documented handover path.
clarify: Rob and the team must confirm task applicability, required lifecycle fields and who may verify/remove/release. The prototype does not establish a real-world isolation policy.

title: Production timestamps can contradict the recorded release chronology
observed: On the live demo, an Electrical lock is recorded from 06:10 until 14:00 and release is recorded at 14:00. The Operator can then submit first good part at 12:00. The event closes and displays 415 downtime minutes from its 05:05 stop, even though 12:00 falls within the recorded lock interval.
why: The action happens after release, but its stored event time says production resumed before release. The duration arithmetic is correct for its inputs; those inputs are inconsistent with the safety record.
classification: Requirements issue: FR-005 constrains time relative to stop, and FR-015 constrains the current permission to confirm. Neither explicitly constrains the entered historical production time relative to release or recorded isolation intervals. Do not label the missing temporal rule a proven violation of an unambiguous coded requirement.
change: Specify chronology invariants for stop, isolation, removal, authorization and first good part. For a LOTO event, reject production times earlier than the valid release or within an active isolation interval. If retrospective corrections are needed, define distinct event/recording times and a reviewed correction workflow.
retest: After release at 14:00, first good part at 12:00 must be refused with a chronology message; a valid time at/after release succeeds. Existing earlier-than-stop and future-time tests must remain.
clarify: Confirm with Angela and Rob whether retrospective production times and corrections are permitted and which timestamps are authoritative.

title: A new breakdown disappears while an earlier event awaits paperwork closure
observed: Press 17 stops at 06:55, first good part is confirmed at 07:10, and its reason/closure are left pending. At 07:25, Simulate another stop reselects the old r5 event. The stop remains 06:55, first good part remains 07:10 and downtime remains frozen at 15 minutes. No new stop interval is created.
why: The system treats unclosed paperwork as an ongoing stop even after production resumed. The interviews explicitly include reason codes entered later, so resumed production with incomplete paperwork is plausible. Accurate event and repeat-fault records cannot depend on instant administrative closure.
classification: Requirements issue: FR-003 says one open event and US1-3 deduplicates another stop while it is open, but open is not separated from currently stopped. The implementation obeys that rule literally. It is insufficient for the machine-event goal after production resumes.
change: Separate the downtime interval from repair/work-order completion. Permit a fresh stop after a recorded first good part, even if earlier coding or closeout is pending. Define the invariant as one active stop interval per machine and deduplicate only signals within that same active interval. Preserve links to related repair work.
retest: Resume at 07:10, leave the reason pending, and stop at 07:25: a fresh running interval must appear while the first interval retains 15 minutes. Repeated signals while the machine remains stopped must still deduplicate.
clarify: Angela and Teo should confirm how stop intervals, work orders and recurrence relate when closure is delayed.

title: A current-shift note clears the overdue handover obligation
observed: At 06:30 Molder 8 is Not acknowledged. Maya saves a normal finding without clicking Acknowledge handover. The view becomes Current shift, the acknowledgment button and overdue state disappear, and the acknowledgment count remains zero.
why: Entering work and accepting responsibility for the prior shift are different actions. The demo no longer exposes a missing explicit acknowledgment once someone edits the record.
classification: Requirements issue / specification inconsistency: FR-016 and the clarification base eligibility on latest work time, while FR-017 describes a deadline for an unacknowledged event. The implementation follows latest-work eligibility. The team must decide whether a note is intended to count as implicit acceptance before treating this as a coding defect.
change: Define a pending handover per dated shift occurrence or responsibility transfer. Keep it pending until explicit authorized acknowledgment; ordinary entries must not erase it. Define whether changed critical isolation data after acknowledgment requires a new acknowledgment.
retest: After the 06:30 deadline, save a current-shift note: the handover remains pending/highlighted with zero acknowledgments. Explicit acknowledgment records actor/time and clears the obligation.
clarify: Confirm with Rob and Angela whether explicit acceptance is required and whether a Technician can satisfy the incoming-supervisor goal in this demo.

title: No matching reason code is treated as proof that the machine ran a full shift
observed: A Hydraulic repair has first good part at 06:10 and its verification deadline is 22:00. The press stops again at 07:00 and never records another first good part. At 22:05, coding that ongoing stop Electrical/Heater makes the earlier repair say Verified – ran full Swing shift. The machine was recorded as stopped throughout that shift. The independent probe reproduces the same case for Day shift.
why: The code can establish absence of a same-category recorded repeat, not a full operating shift or successful verification cycle. A reason category is also a broad proxy for fault identity. These are different levels of evidence.
classification: Requirements issue: FR-018/019 and the confirm-with-Teo assumption explicitly use same machine plus reason code. The implementation largely follows that algorithm; the criterion and display claim do not establish the stated stakeholder goal.
change: Distinguish Awaiting evidence, No matching recurrence observed and Verified repair. Define what counts as a full operating shift and require appropriate run/verification evidence, such as a recorded verification outcome or operating interval. Define a better fault identity or explicitly retain the limitations of category matching.
retest: An unrelated stop covering the required shift must prevent a Ran full shift claim. A complete operating/verification interval can verify the repair; a matching fault reopens it; an uncoded stop keeps classification pending.
clarify: Teo must confirm the verification horizon and evidence, and whether same reason code reliably identifies a repeat fault.
